lines.li: [us] What's it like at {TOWN}?
[them,their:tribal] Drying racks, a long fire, and hides stacked higher than my head.
[them,their:medieval] A row of stalls under one roof, a weighbeam, and a tithe box by the door.
[them,their:empire] A clean station, a counting room, and an imperial banner kept bright as new.
[them,their:spacer] A landing pad, two sealed stores, and a counter with a scanner on it.
[them,their:industrial] A warehouse, a loading dock, and a stove in the office that never warms it.
[them] A store, a yard for the carts, and more coming and going than you'd think.
[us] Sounds busy.
[them,town:struggling|town:poor] It sounds busier than it is, most weeks.
[them] Busy enough, and busier when your people come.
[them] I keep the {POSTKIND} at {TOWN}, so I know most of your people by their faces.
[us] And by what they buy?
[them,their:medieval] Aye, and by what they haggle over, which is everything.
[them,their:empire] I know what each of them needs, which in a well-run station is the same thing.
[them,their:tribal] By what they bring, and whether the hides were scraped clean.
[them] That too, and by who pays on time.

ColonyCouncil.OutsiderTalkDef.heard: The colony's people are known at {TOWN}, the {POSTKIND} of {PEOPLE}.

lines.li: [us] Who keeps the {POSTKIND} at {TOWN} these days?
[them] {KEEPER}, still, and welcome to the books.
[us] Is {KEEPER} fair to work for?
[them,their:empire] Correct to the coin, which is not the same as fair, but close.
[them,their:tribal] Fair as the elders, and twice as hard to fool.
[them] Fair enough, and tight with a wage.
[them] Winter at {TOWN} is counting stock and listening for carts that don't come.
[us] Do you go home for it?
[them,their:tribal] Some do, but the fire at the trading camp is never left alone.
[them] Some do, but someone always stays behind with the stock.
[them] The first carts of spring reach {TOWN} with mud up to the axles.
[us] Anything good on them?
[them] Seed and salt, and a whole season's news from home.
[them] Summer is when {TOWN} earns its keep, with the roads dry and buyers on them.
[us] Including us.
[them] Especially you, the place was opened for you.
[them] Before the roads go bad we send the last loads home from {TOWN}.
[us] What goes back?
[them,their:tribal] What your people traded us, and the elders' share of the hides.
[them] Whatever your people sold us, mostly, and the books for the year.
[them] The post is a long way from the rest of our people, and the evenings show it.
[us] What do you do with them?
[them,their:tribal] Tell the old stories twice, to make them last.
[them,their:spacer] Run the inventory again and call it company.
[them,their:medieval] Dice, and a song if the factor's in a good mood.
[them] Cards, mostly, and letters home that take a month to get there.
[them] I brought my children out to {TOWN}, and they think the road is the whole world.
[us] Do they like it there?
[them] They like the days your people come best, it's the only crowd they ever see.
[us] Do they haggle at {TOWN} the way the caravans do?
[them] Worse, we've got all day and nowhere else to be.
[us] That's not reassuring.
[them] It wasn't meant to be.
[us] Is {TOWN} safe, with your people at war?
[them] We keep a watch on the road and the gate shut after dark.
[us] Will that do?
[them] It does until the day it doesn't, so we keep the stock low.
[them] With things as they are at home, the carts out to {TOWN} come half empty.
[us] Does that hurt trade at the post?
[them] It does, and it'll mend when home does.
[us] How is the {POSTKIND} doing?
[them] Steady, which for a post this far from home is high praise.
[us] We'll keep coming.
[them] Good, we'd rather see the same faces than none.
[them] The depot at {TOWN} has a radio, so we hear the prices from home the same day.
[us] Do they change much?
[them] Every day, and always the wrong way for whoever's buying.
[them] The ground station at {TOWN} logs every sale, every landing and every complaint.
[us] Any complaints about us?
[them] Two, both about the mud on your boots.
[them] The elders chose {KEEPER} to keep the trading camp, because {KEEPER} forgets no debt.
[us] Not even a small one?
[them] The small ones least of all.
[them] Market day at {TOWN} draws farmers from farther off than you'd believe.
[us] All that way for a market?
[them] For a market and a fight after it, if the ale holds out.
[them] I hold this station by the court's leave, and I mean to prove the court chose well.
[us] How do you show that?
[them] With full stores, clean books, and your colony's custom.
[them] Your face is known at {TOWN}, you're one of the regulars.
[us] I'm there often enough.
[them,their:tribal] Then come when the moon is full, that's when the best hides come in.
[them,their:medieval] Then come on market day, when the good cloth is out.
[them] Then you know the good stock goes early.
[us,tribal] When we go to {TOWN}, it's a trading party on foot with the hides on our backs.
[us,medieval] When we go to {TOWN}, it's a pack train and a long day of mules complaining.
[us,spacer] When we go to {TOWN}, it's a supply run, in and out.
[us] When we go to {TOWN}, it's a caravan and a long road.
[them] Long or short, it's shorter than it was before the post.
[them] A season behind the counter at {TOWN}, and I needed a few nights under another roof.
[us] Ours will do?
[them] Yours has fewer crates in it, so yes.
[them] I wrote that letter about closing {TOWN}, and I didn't enjoy writing it.
[us] We read it.
[them,tone:warm|tone:good] Then let's both see that I never have to send the next one.
[them] Then you know where things stand.
[them] Some at {TOWN} have started sorting what they'd carry home first.
[us] It hasn't come to that.
[them] No, but the ones packing say it never hurts to be ready.
[them] Make the most of {TOWN} while it's open.
[us] Is it closing?
[them] That's for your colony to decide, not me.
[them] We opened {TOWN} for you, and look how that's going.
[us] That isn't only our doing.
[them] Have you been out to {POST} yet, our people's {POSTKIND}?
[us] We know the way.
[them,their:tribal] Good, the elders opened it so your feet would wear a path there.
[them] Good, it was opened with your colony in mind.
[them] Our people keep {POST} near you, and it isn't cheap for them.
[us] Then why keep it?
[them] Ask the ones who opened it, I only pay for it.
[them] The young ones at home all want a turn at {POST}, it's the farthest any of us get.
[us] Is it so far?
[them,their:lowtech] Far enough that they come back with stories, and that's what they want.
[them] Far enough to come back with stories, which is the whole point at that age.
[them] {POSTPEOPLE} keep a post at {POST}, so I suppose I'm the dear option now.
[us] You came to the gate, though.
[them] That's the one thing I've got on them.
[them] The traders at {POST} build walls around their goods, as if goods could run off.
[us] It keeps the rain out.
[them] Rain never hurt a good hide.
[them] {POSTPEOPLE} keep a post at {POST}, and I'd like to know who they pay for the road.
[us] Not that we know of.
[them] Then somebody will be asking them before long.
[them] I passed the post at {POST} on the way here, and it lacks a proper wall.
[us] It's a trading post.
[them] Then I hope its traders are quicker than its builders.
[them] Your colony razed the post our people opened for it.
[us] I won't defend it here.
[them] Good, because at home they wouldn't listen.
[them] {WRONGNAME} was opened for your people, and your people razed it.
[us] We did, and I won't deny it.
